Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Onkar Singh,
Sachin Malik
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Vivek Kumar Tiwari Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for the informant and learned AGA for the State and perused the record.

2. The present bail application has been filed by the applicant in Case Crime No. 55 of 2022, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 506 IPC, P.S.- Civil Lines, District- Meerut, with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.

3. As per allegations contained in the F.I.R., the accused persons namely Shaukeen, Dilshad and Nayab came to the informant on 10.03.2020 and asked him to buy a plot measuring 100 sq. yards and cajoled him to enter into the transaction.

One of them, namely, Nayab took Rs.1,65,000/- as commission and a total of Rs.16,50,000/- was paid to them and they assured that the sale deed will Dilshad Kureshi vs State Of U.P. on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38090328/
1 be executed within 10 days.

sentences.text: Later they refused to execute the same and instead offered another plot of 200 sq. yards at a different place at price of Rs.43,00,000/-.
The informant paid rest of the amount Rs.26,50,000/-.
When he reached at the plot, he came to know that his plot was already sold to a person named Adil and that informant was defrauded to the tune of Rs.43,00,000/-.
4. It is further submitted that dispute between the parties is purely civil in nature and earlier a compromise was also arrived at between the parties.
The opposite party no.2 has already initiated proceedings under Section 138 N.I. Act.

It was submitted that similarly placed co-accused, namely,
Nayab Tantrik @ Nayab Khan and Mohd. Shaukin Tantrik have already been granted anticipatory bail by Co-ordinate Benches of this Court.

The applicant was also granted interim anticipatory bail by this Court vide order dated 03.01.2023 but said interim order could not be extended further, due to which non-bailable warrants were issued against him and now applicant is in jail since 15.04.2025.
The applicant has no previous criminal history.

Referring to facts of the matter, it was submitted that there is no credible evidence against applicant and in case applicant is granted bail,
he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and would co-operate during trial.

5. Learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant have opposed the prayer of bail and submitted that in the alleged incident informant has been cheated by the applicant and co-accused persons to the tune of Rs.43 lakhs on pretext of selling land.

Learned counsel for the informant has referred facts of the matter and submitted that applicant was actively involved in the entire incident and there are serious allegations against him and he is not entitled for bail.
6. I have considered rival submissions and perused the record.
7. It is well settled that at pre-conviction stage, there is presumption of innocence.
The object of keeping a person in custody is to ensure his availability to face the trial and to receive the sentence that may be passed.
The detention is not supposed to be punitive or preventive.
Seriousness of the allegation or the availability of material in support thereof are not the only considerations for declining bail.

In this connection reference may be made to case of Vinod Bhandari Vs State of M.P.
(2015) 11 Supreme Court Cases 502.
8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations, period of detention and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits, a case for bail is made out.
According bail application is allowed.

9. Let the applicant Dilshad Kureshi, involved in aforesaid case crime, be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:
(i). The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii). The applicant shall not pressurize / intimidate the prosecution witness.
Dilshad Kureshi vs State Of U.P. on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38090328/
2 (iii).

entities.text: Dilshad Kureshi vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicant shall appear before the Trial Court on the date fixed, unless his personal appearance is exempted.

(iv). The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court.
10.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the Court concerned shall be at liberty to cancel bail of applicant in accordance with law.
